messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] [stan-users] Numerical Problems in MCMC Metropolis Simulation
parts:
This is all addressed in the integration time paper.

To briefly summarize, let theta_{0} be the initial
point and let ( \theta_{0}, \ldots, \theta_{N} ) be
an ensemble of proposals including the initial
point.

There are numerous ways of choosing a point
from this ensemble while maintaining the correct
invariant distribution.

We could multinomially sample each point using the weights

p( theta_{n} ) = pi( theta_{n} ) / ( sum_{m = 0}^{N} pi( theta_{m} )

Or we could slice sample by sampling a threshold

u \sim U(0, \pi(theta_{0} )

and then uniformly sample from the points in the
ensemble with densities above this threshold,

theta_{new} \sim U( theta_{n} | pi(theta_{n}) > u ).

Both of these procedures generate leave the exact
target distribution invariant, and hence when applied
to HMC exactly correct for any error in the symplectic
integrator.
